name: Closed-Uncertainty semantic retrieval baseline
description: Eight manually labelled retrieval questions covering uncertainty formulation, evaluation, failure mechanisms, calibration, learned error prediction, and held-out human CT evaluation.

cases.question: Under fixed Gaussian geometry, why can radiative CT rendering support one-pass analytic predictive moments, and what normalization is required for squared projected kernels?
Which complementary metrics evaluate whether uncertainty identifies reconstruction error, and how is the foreground region defined?
How much does uncertainty ranking deteriorate when evaluation is restricted from the entire volume to the object foreground, and what does successful temperature calibration fail to repair?
Why can disagreement across repeated reconstructions fail to reveal the dominant reconstruction error, and does correcting the predictive-mean offset fix the spatial ranking?
Why do scalar temperature or conformal calibration not improve spatial error localization, and what change to the reconstruction members produced better ranking?
What explains apparently strong full-volume uncertainty scores despite weak error localization inside the reconstructed object?
Which test-time features are used to predict error missed by posterior spread, and how well does the learned predictor transfer to other view budgets, reconstruction backbones, and real scans?
How was evaluation on held-out human anatomy designed, and what improvements did anatomy-trained predictors achieve for foreground ranking and selective prediction?
